title: The Will of the Marlowe Estate
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Marlowe is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, night-shift taxi dispatcher Odile Halloran realizes the fare logs she's kept for years contain coded entries tied to the Marlowe estate. As she decodes the ledger, she uncovers a decades-old cover-up: Edmund never died—he was smuggled out by his own family, and the estate's power has rested on that lie ever since. Odile, once invisible, becomes both target and witness, forced to choose between protecting the man she's quietly loved and exposing the truth before the statute of limitations expires. In the end, she publishes the ledger, toppling the Marlowe heirs, while Edmund—still alive, ancient and unrepentant—dies free, leaving her the only honest inheritance: the truth itself.
about_author: S. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent fifteen years listening to secrets before writing them down. They live in New England with two cats and an unhealthy interest in probate law.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working the graveyard shift at Halloran Taxi, Odile overhears police radio chatter about the exhumation of founder Edmund Marlowe. By dawn, the news breaks: the coffin is empty. The beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Fare 447
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reviewing old dispatch logs to distract herself, Odile finds a recurring anonymous fare, #447, picked up near the Marlowe cemetery on the night Edmund 'died'—paid in cash, destination redacted. Emotional beat: the first cold thrill of pattern recognition.

chapters.title: The Heirs Assemble
chapters.summary: Dual POV shifting to Vivian Marlowe-Cross, Edmund's imperious granddaughter, who convenes the family as lawyers descend on the estate. Vivian orders the family archivist to burn certain papers. Beat: power flexing, corruption introduced from above.

chapters.title: Night Routes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She maps every Fare 447 across thirty years onto a chart of the town and finds they cluster around the derelict Marlowe boathouse. Her supervisor warns her to drop it. Beat: loyalty tested—her boss may be on someone's payroll.

chapters.title: A Man Called Wren
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A new regular passenger, Elias Wren, an estate groundskeeper, begins riding her cab at odd hours. Their conversations are careful, charged; he knows more than he says about the exhumation. Beat: love interest introduced against her better judgment.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cross-referencing fare numbers with hymn numbers from the Marlowe memorial chapel, Odile cracks the first layer: the dispatch book is a cipher keyed to the chapel's hymnal. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by fear of what the code protects.

chapters.title: What Vivian Burned
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. The archivist, guilt-ridden, hides one box instead of burning it. Vivian suspects a leak inside the household and hires a fixer, Dane Kessler. Beat: menace tightening; the reader sees the hunters mobilize.

chapters.title: The Boathouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile and Wren search the boathouse and find a hidden room: bedding, medicine bottles, decades of newspapers—a life lived in hiding. Someone has been living there until very recently. Beat: awe curdling into vertigo.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A retired clerk explains the legal clock: fraud claims against the estate expire in ninety days unless new evidence surfaces. Odile realizes the ledger is her only weapon—and her death warrant. Beat: stakes made explicit, ticking clock installed.

chapters.title: Kessler's Card
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fixer Dane Kessler rides in her cab, leaves a card, and makes a generous offer for her dispatch archives. She refuses; by morning her apartment has been searched. Beat: violation and defiance—she stops being a bystander.

chapters.title: Wren's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren admits he was hired years ago to care for a hidden occupant of the boathouse—Edmund himself, alive into extreme old age. He never knew why, only that the family paid him to forget. Beat: betrayal and tenderness entangled; trust nearly breaks.

chapters.title: The Hymnal Key
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Decoding deeper, Odile finds entries describing payments, a faked death certificate signed by the town doctor, and a second name: not Edmund, but his twin brother, buried under Edmund's name—or so the code implies. Beat: the mystery doubles back on itself.

chapters.title: Doctor's Orders
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Vivian confronts the aging doctor's widow, who produces the real death certificate and blackmails her. Vivian orders Kessler to handle it permanently. Beat: corruption compounding; the moral floor drops away.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The taxi company's archive room burns overnight. Odile survives an ambush in the parking lot thanks to Wren's warning call. Beat: terror and gratitude fuse; she and Wren become co-conspirators in truth.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Box
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The guilt-stricken family archivist contacts Odile through the cab company and surrenders the unburned box: correspondence proving Edmund orchestrated his own disappearance to escape debts and let his heirs inherit a myth. Beat: revelation with bitter irony—the beloved founder was the first corruptor.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren is offered money and immunity to testify that Odile fabricated the ledger. Torn between the family that employed him and the woman he loves, he burns his contract and chooses her. Beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty redirected toward truth.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Day Eighty-Nine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With hours left, Odile files the decoded ledger with the county clerk and tips a state investigative journalist. Kessler corners her at the courthouse steps; Wren intervenes, and Kessler is arrested on outstanding warrants. Beat: climax—courage at the deadline's edge.

chapters.title: The Man in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Summoned by a final Fare 447 entry, Odile finds Edmund himself, 104 years old, hiding in the chapel crypt. He offers her anything to stay silent one more week. She refuses—not out of hate, but because the town deserves its own name back. Beat: face-to-face with the source of everything.

chapters.title: Edmund's Last Ride
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Edmund, dying, asks for one last fare. Odile drives him herself along the route he coded into her ledger all those years. He dies in the back seat as the story breaks on every radio station—including hers. Beat: elegiac, strange mercy; the lie dies with its author.

chapters.title: Probate and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. The estate collapses: indictments, asset freezes, Vivian's public disgrace. She finally reads her grandfather's letters and understands she inherited nothing but a performance. Beat: downfall without cheap villainy—grief for a false legacy.

chapters.title: The Second Burial
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Edmund is buried properly, under his own name, in a small service Odile attends uninvited and unremarked. Wren stands beside her. The town begins rewriting its founding story. Beat: resolution, mourning what was believed rather than what was true.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue. Months later, Odile still works nights, but now teaches a community class on local history using the ledger. A new anonymous fare request comes in—destination: the boathouse. She smiles, assigns herself, and drives toward whatever comes next. Beat: earned hope; visibility chosen at last.
